en: Hetusampayuttaduka (The Pair on Association with Roots)
Dependent on a state associated with non-root-cause (nahetusampayutta), a state associated with non-root-cause arises by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya).
Dependent on a state associated with non-root-cause, a state dissociated from non-root-cause (nahetuvippayutta) arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state associated with non-root-cause, states both associated with non-root-cause and dissociated from non-root-cause arise...
They arise by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).
Dependent on a state that is neither-root-nor-dissociated, a state that is neither-root-nor-dissociated arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root-nor-dissociated, a state that is neither-root-yet-associated arises by way of the root condition.

Dependent on a state that is not associated with a root (*nahetuvippayutta*), there arise states that are both associated with a root and not associated with a root by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is both associated with a root and not associated with a root, there arises a state that is associated with a root by way of the root condition… three [combinations]. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-cause, nine; in the case of object, six; in the case of predominance, five ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance, nine. (This should be expanded in full everywhere—in the section on conascence, ... pe ... and in the section on inquiry.)
